about.greeting: I am a fullstack developer with a strong bias toward quality and data. I started out reading data, learned how production breaks while working in support, and since 2022 I have been building software from the database to the interface — understanding the problem before picking the tool.
about.professionalDescription: Today I work fullstack at Stech, with TypeScript, React, NestJS and Prisma over MySQL. Before that: Java and Spring Boot at Persys, conversion-focused frontend at Make and test engineering at Outlier, evaluating models across voice, vision and text. I also taught Excel, Power BI and generative AI at Cebrac.
about.expertiseDescription: What I bring to a team is judgement, not a stack list: fixing vulnerabilities before they become incidents, turning business rules into traceable parameters and treating Core Web Vitals as a requirement — the bar behind more than a hundred landing pages. TaskForge cut 70% to 90% of the engineering LLM bill.

portal_remuneracao_frota.title: Payroll and fleet portal
portal_remuneracao_frota.description: Internal portal for monthly payroll closing, fleet mileage, base records and reports, built on Lumen and React with TypeScript. The case is measurement: the closing screen fired 354 queries per load and ten of the eleven domain tables had no index at all, with 293 thousand rows in full scan. Seven indexes derived from the measured predicates took the screen from 4,271 ms to 354 ms with a byte-identical response; the remaining N+1 was mapped at 316 of the 354 queries. It also produced deploy-hygiene fixes: a config file pointing at localhost kept out of the commit, and a backup .env the gitignore did not cover. Client under confidentiality: no name, repository or screenshot.

servidor_llm_local.title: Self-hosted LLM server
servidor_llm_local.description: Internal server turned into a local model host and file store. Ubuntu 24.04 on bare metal, Docker with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and the GPU visible inside the container; Ollama serving an 8B model over the local API. Remote access through Tailscale rather than an internet-facing port, and authenticated Samba shares with no guest access. Sizing was stated alongside the delivery: this hardware profile serves RAG and quantised 7B/8B models, not heavy multi-user inference.

decision.title: How this decision was made
decision.selfReported: Figure reported by Augusto, with no measurement attached. Either the measurement shows up, or the figure goes.

payroll.context: The monthly closing screen fired 354 queries per load, including full scans over 293 thousand rows.
payroll.constraint: Ten of the eleven domain tables had no index, while the response had to remain byte-identical.
payroll.decision: Create seven indexes derived from the measured predicates and map the remaining N+1.
payroll.evidence: The response was compared byte-for-byte after the change; the remaining N+1 was identified in 316 of the 354 queries.
payroll.impact: Screen time dropped from 4,271 ms to 354 ms.
payroll.proves: Optimisation proven by measurement, not by feel: the response was compared byte for byte before and after, so the tenfold gain did not come from changing what the screen returns.

stechclub.proves: Security as an architecture decision, not a warning: the bucket key never reaches the browser because media is served through the API. The domain model survived the scope tripling, from static course to tracks and playlists.
stechclub.context: Education portal in two sub-projects, a React SPA and a NestJS API, with a public landing page and an authenticated area for courses, tracks and videos.
stechclub.constraint: The company already had its own SSO, and course video cannot be served straight from the bucket.
stechclub.decision: Reuse corporate SSO instead of reimplementing auth, address media by hash under separate prefixes, and hand out links through an authenticated API.
stechclub.evidence: A SHA256 per stored object recorded in the database; Swagger and Redoc documenting the API; unit and E2E Jest tests; a health endpoint reporting database state.
stechclub.impact: No bucket credential ever reaches the client, and the model absorbed tracks, playlists and class material without a domain rewrite.

asurapadel.proves: The most complete performance case in this portfolio: symptom, diagnosis, four lines of attack and a number. It is also recent Angular over a C# backend on Azure.
asurapadel.context: Padel court management split into two applications in one repository: an Angular frontend and a C# REST API deployed to Azure App Service.
asurapadel.constraint: The bottleneck only surfaced once the API left the local machine for the test server, serving a base of 4,000 to 10,000 clients.
asurapadel.decision: Attack on four fronts at once — caching, endpoint redesign, payload reduction and frontend optimisation — and paginate in fragmented batches instead of returning everything in one response.
asurapadel.evidence: Pagination became an API contract decision, not a UI one; consumption configured per environment, with dev, test and production pointing at distinct APIs; test coverage reported at 88% with Jest and JUnit.
asurapadel.impact: Average response time reported dropping from 800 ms to 220 ms, roughly 72%.

portal_agente_ia.proves: Quality control applied to a non-deterministic system. Versioning the prompt with rollback and isolating the test channel from the live one are QA decisions about AI, not conveniences.
portal_agente_ia.context: A portal that lets a non-technical operator run, test and audit an AI support agent connected to WhatsApp. The product is not the agent: it is the interface that makes it operable.
portal_agente_ia.constraint: The automation behind the agent was barely modifiable, and test traffic could not mix with real support conversations.
portal_agente_ia.decision: Add prompt versioning with rollback, route the sandbox through a separate webhook, and keep credentials and integrations in a managed backend, outside the browser.
portal_agente_ia.evidence: Uploads and catalogue processed into a vector store with queue state and traceability visible in the portal; conversation logs and the upload queue behind an authenticated function.
portal_agente_ia.impact: Operators can change the agent behaviour and roll it back on their own, and no test ever contaminates a customer conversation.

suite_financeira_b2b.proves: The closest thing here to a financial system at scale, and the only one with all three layers together: transactional, asynchronous and analytical. Kafka here has a topic per domain, a DLQ and per-environment deployments.
suite_financeira_b2b.context: A financial operations suite across three repositories: an admin and API backend, a web interface and data pipelines, covering operations, assignments, portfolios, criteria, approvals and integrations.
suite_financeira_b2b.constraint: A domain event cannot be lost, and an operation file cannot be served from an open URL.
suite_financeira_b2b.decision: Split transactional from asynchronous and analytical work, with Kafka topics per domain and a dead letter queue, presigned URLs for every file and secrets in a managed vault.
suite_financeira_b2b.evidence: Consumers with error handling and a DLQ, per-environment deployments across staging, homologation and production, presigned URLs in inconsistency notifications and file returns, and dependency auditing with pip-audit in the build and test job.
suite_financeira_b2b.impact: The dependency chain is audited in CI and no operation file is ever exposed through a direct link.

servidor_llm_local.proves: Infrastructure with a declared exposure boundary: internal services never face the internet, sharing refuses guests, and the machine capacity is stated as it is rather than as it would sell.
servidor_llm_local.context: Turning a desktop into a file server, a local LLM host and a visual workstation, on a Ryzen 3 with 24 GB of RAM and a 12 GB RTX 3060.
servidor_llm_local.constraint: The same machine has to drive a graphical interface, and nothing may be exposed directly to the internet.
servidor_llm_local.decision: Ubuntu Desktop on bare metal instead of Server, a local runtime with Docker and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, remote access only over a private network, and authenticated sharing with no guest share.
servidor_llm_local.evidence: GPU recognised inside the container, inference validated with an 8B model over a local API, and directories separated by group permission.
servidor_llm_local.impact: The profile is recorded as fit for storage, RAG and quantised 7B–8B models — and explicitly not sold as heavy multi-user inference.

mitra_crm.proves: Software delivered to a real business, with usage data, nine tables and an executable release — the step that separates a study project from a product someone else operates.
mitra_crm.context: A desktop CRM with quote generation for a curtains and blinds company, in Python with tkinter and SQLite.
mitra_crm.constraint: The people using it do not install a development environment: the deliverable has to be an executable.
mitra_crm.decision: Model nine tables instead of single-entity CRUD, package with PyInstaller, and abandon the MVC restructuring midway, keeping the reason on record.
mitra_crm.evidence: Three tracked iterations — a customer-module prototype, an abandoned MVC attempt and the final product — with pytest tests and around 30 generated quotes, largely test data.
mitra_crm.impact: Reported reduction of roughly 45% in report generation time, through query optimisation.

taskforge.proves: It sets the agent autonomy boundary before optimising for speed: a read-only planner, no agent ever pushes, merge stays human. That is QA applied to AI as design, not as a warning.
taskforge.context: Meta-tooling that turns a request into a task DAG and runs agents in parallel waves, one Git worktree per task.
taskforge.constraint: An agent writing to a shared repository is a risk: a solo publish has to be impossible, not merely unlikely.
taskforge.decision: Split planning from execution, keep the planner read-only, isolate every task in its own branch and worktree, and leave review and merge to a person.
taskforge.evidence: Guards for commitless branches and for histories with no common ancestor; process skills with built-in gates — approval before execution, 80% minimum coverage and reversible migrations; four interfaces over one engine, sharing plans on disk.
taskforge.impact: The thesis stopped being "run agents" and became mapping how the team works, then attaching agents only where they fit.

omegahub.proves: Domain modularisation on the backend and a typed end-to-end contract — plus two payment providers in one flow, which is a real abstraction problem, not an exercise.
omegahub.context: A gaming platform in a monorepo, with Next.js on the frontend and NestJS over Fastify on the backend.
omegahub.constraint: Two payment providers have to coexist in the same purchase flow without leaking the difference into the rest of the system.
omegahub.decision: Separate Store, Orders and Payments as independent domains, expose a typed end-to-end contract with tRPC, and push asynchronous work onto queues.
omegahub.evidence: BullMQ queues over Redis for work outside the request cycle.
omegahub.impact: Swapping or adding a payment provider stays contained inside the Payments domain, never reaching Store or Orders.

pronto.proves: Architecture chosen by product stage, with the trade-offs named: PostGIS versus Redis GEO, Kafka versus pg-boss, payment split versus manual transfer. One card, two phases, no portfolio padding.
pronto.context: An urgent-services marketplace in two phases: an operationally cheap MVP and an architectural evolution for scale.
pronto.constraint: The MVP has to be cheap to run; the next phase has to take volume and work offline-first.
pronto.decision: Compare every piece instead of picking the most modern one: geolocation, queueing and payment were each decided twice, once per phase, with the reason recorded.
pronto.impact: The comparison shows how the design shifts between MVP and scale, without becoming two separate portfolio entries.

barbearia_app.proves: Consistency under concurrency solved in the data layer, with an exclusion constraint, instead of application-level retries. Geolocation on an open stack instead of a proprietary map service.
barbearia_app.context: A discovery and booking PWA for barbershops, with a map, real-time slots and three user roles.
barbearia_app.constraint: Two customers cannot book the same slot, and the race happens at the moment of booking.
barbearia_app.decision: Prevent the overlap with a database exclusion constraint, and use Leaflet, OpenStreetMap and PostGIS instead of a proprietary map service.
barbearia_app.impact: The guarantee no longer depends on the application retrying: the database refuses the second booking.

pasta_la_vista.proves: Databases chosen by data shape rather than one database out of convenience, with the rationale recorded in the repository itself. Integration testing was a premise, not an afterthought.
pasta_la_vista.context: A delivery app with Clean Architecture, an Expo mobile client and an Express API.
pasta_la_vista.constraint: Orders, catalogue and sessions have different shapes and lifetimes; and payment confirmation arrives later, by webhook.
pasta_la_vista.decision: Polyglot persistence — PostgreSQL, MongoDB and Redis, each for the shape of the data — and the payment webhook treated as a genuinely asynchronous flow.
pasta_la_vista.evidence: A test compose file separate from the development one, so integration tests run in isolation.
pasta_la_vista.impact: Every database choice is defensible in writing, and payment does not depend on an HTTP response coming back.

buscajogos.proves: A long team project with a stack switch under deadline pressure — an engineering decision with a recorded rationale, not a preference. It is the honest answer to "tell me about changing course mid-project".
buscajogos.context: A team capstone project: a digital game price comparator, graded 9.0 out of 10.
buscajogos.constraint: The deadline was fixed and the stack chosen at the start did not hold the scope.
buscajogos.decision: Switch stacks mid-project, with the reason recorded, instead of dragging the initial choice to delivery.
buscajogos.evidence: The sequence of four frontends is preserved as a trace of real iteration.
buscajogos.impact: Delivered and graded 9.0, with the change of course documented rather than hidden.

kitbuilder.proves: Backend discipline applied where it was not required: repositories and migrations in an academic desktop project, with stock modelled through kit composition.
kitbuilder.context: Layered Python inventory management for electronic components, delivered as the degree capstone.
kitbuilder.constraint: A kit is composed of parts that also exist loose in stock, and the schema shifts over the project.
kitbuilder.decision: Separate data access into repositories and version the schema with migrations, in a context where nobody demanded either.
kitbuilder.impact: The academic project ended up with the structure of a maintained service, not of a course submission.

youtcatcher.proves: Over 80% coverage in a personal app, where nobody was asking for tests. Alongside it, packaging for three operating systems and scripted environment recreation — reproducibility, not "works on my machine".
youtcatcher.context: A desktop YouTube downloader in Python, with strict MVC.
youtcatcher.constraint: A personal project has no reviewer: if quality is not in the process, it does not exist.
youtcatcher.decision: Keep MVC strict, write tests as part of the work, and package for three operating systems.
youtcatcher.evidence: Test coverage above 80% and a script that recreates the virtual environment.
youtcatcher.impact: The app runs outside the machine it was built on, which is the difference between a project and a delivery.

sudoku_solver.proves: The only C/C++ and the only computer vision work here. Splitting a dependency-free solver from a heavy vision layer is a boundary decision, not a language accident.
sudoku_solver.context: A pipeline that solves Sudoku from a photo: the solver in pure C, the vision in C++ with OpenCV.
sudoku_solver.constraint: The solver has to be testable and portable; the vision layer drags in a large dependency.
sudoku_solver.decision: Keep the solver in C with no dependencies at all and isolate OpenCV in the vision layer, on the other side of the boundary.
sudoku_solver.impact: The pure algorithm runs and can be verified without installing computer vision for nothing.

jarbas.proves: A desktop product with an authenticated local protocol: a token generated at boot, a discovery file with restricted permissions, and a 401 on everything but health. Local-service security treated like exposed-service security.
jarbas.context: An operable second brain over any markdown vault with a declared convention, built as an engine plus interfaces.
jarbas.constraint: Nothing may be hardcoded for one specific vault, and a local daemon is still attack surface.
jarbas.decision: A schema-first contract instead of a fixed structure, a mandatory session token outside health, CORS restricted to the interface origins, and decisions formalised as ADRs.
jarbas.evidence: A suite of 145 green tests, a resolved wikilink graph of 478 nodes and 1,631 edges on the validation vault, and reindexing with live progress.
jarbas.impact: The engine serves any vault that declares the schema, and the interface talks to it over an authenticated contract.

quinto_selo.proves: Automated headless verification of an online multiplayer game, with assertions counted in the log — not "I opened it and it did not break". Netcode validated before judging feel.
quinto_selo.context: A two-player online co-op roguelite in Godot 4, written in typed GDScript.
quinto_selo.constraint: The machine has 8 GB of RAM, and network behaviour is not proven by opening the game and looking.
quinto_selo.decision: A compatibility renderer because of the memory limit, the host simulating both bodies with the client interpolating on top, and a two-stage headless suite — unit plus integration with host and bot.
quinto_selo.evidence: 42 assertions enforced against the process logs; two defects came out of the first play window and were fixed.
quinto_selo.impact: The netcode slice and the two-body death slice closed with reproducible verification, not with an impression.

financeos.proves: Structural debt measured, not estimated: the code graph itself points at low cohesion in two places and 274 weakly connected nodes. Technical self-criticism with numbers is rare in a portfolio.
financeos.context: A personal finance management monorepo, with Prisma over a relational database and Redis for caching.
financeos.constraint: A personal monorepo grows without an outside reviewer, and poor cohesion only shows up when someone measures.
financeos.decision: Index the code into a graph and read the result, instead of trusting a feeling of tidiness.
financeos.evidence: Around 780 mapped nodes, with low cohesion localised in the workspace store and the Prisma service, plus separate compose files for development and production.
financeos.impact: The debt became an addressed list, which is what makes it attackable by priority instead of by rewrite.

zoologic.proves: One of the few sets of authored tests here, and the one most aligned with my QA stance: it tests controllers and models with failure cases, not just the happy path. It is also the only PHP in this portfolio.
zoologic.context: Zoo management in two sub-projects: a PHP 8 API with SOLID and a Next.js frontend.
zoologic.constraint: A test suite that only covers the happy path proves nothing about how the system fails.
zoologic.decision: Write controller and model tests including failure cases, with PHPUnit, and apply SOLID and layered routing outside the comfort of Node.
zoologic.impact: The suite covers failure, not just success, which is the difference between a test and a demo.

repo_explorer_angular.proves: A senior Angular take-home delivered with justified decisions over feature count: the race condition removed by construction, and tests chosen by risk rather than by coverage.
repo_explorer_angular.context: A repository explorer consuming the public GitHub API, scoped to 3–4 hours, explicitly graded on decisions over features.
repo_explorer_angular.constraint: Type-ahead search produces stale requests, and the public API rate-limits without a token.
repo_explorer_angular.decision: Signals for synchronous and derived state, RxJS for asynchronous flow, and debounce plus distinctUntilChanged plus switchMap to cancel stale requests; rate limiting treated as a first-class error state in the UI.
repo_explorer_angular.evidence: An anchor test over the search pipeline with fake time, covering debounce, cancellation and errors; OnPush on every presentation component; an in-memory cache per term and a countdown reading the reset header; CI with lint, test and build.
repo_explorer_angular.impact: CI green on delivery, and the oral defence happened with a README written to support it.

instagram_analyzer.proves: Reading the local export instead of scraping the platform is a design decision that avoids blocking and third-party data. Data analysis delivered as an interface, not a notebook.
instagram_analyzer.context: A Python desktop app that processes the Instagram JSON export and shows who does not follow back, with KPIs and live search.
instagram_analyzer.constraint: Scraping the platform breaks on blocking and reaches other people data for no reason.
instagram_analyzer.decision: Consume only the export the user downloads themselves, and ship the result as an application with an interface.
instagram_analyzer.impact: It works without depending on an unstable API and without touching data that is not the user own.

pokedex.proves: Persistent local caching in a read-heavy mobile app — the strategy the marketplace projects never had to solve, isolated here in a frontend with no backend of its own.
pokedex.context: An Expo mobile exploration app, with no custom backend.
pokedex.constraint: Repeated queries over slow-changing data should not depend on the network at every launch.
pokedex.decision: Persist locally in SQLite instead of refetching, and animate with a native gesture and motion library.
pokedex.impact: The app opens and responds without a network, and the caching decision is reusable beyond this project.

javafx_pokemon.proves: Java desktop with MVC separation and a Maven build — the counterweight to a mostly web portfolio, inside a track of exercises that crosses platforms with the same domain.
javafx_pokemon.context: A JavaFX desktop application with Maven, as an architecture exercise in Java.
javafx_pokemon.decision: Keep MVC separation and Maven dependency management, instead of a single-file exercise.
javafx_pokemon.impact: The exercise became comparable to the others in the same track, which run on mobile and web over the same domain.

calc_financeira.proves: Financial rules, componentised UI, persisted history and embedded charts in one desktop app — with the internal evolution on record, from a monolithic implementation to an MVC layout.
calc_financeira.context: An income-splitting desktop app with a dashboard, comparisons, history and charts.
calc_financeira.constraint: The first version was monolithic, and building on top of it would get expensive.
calc_financeira.decision: Reorganise into modular MVC while preserving the earlier implementation, instead of erasing the starting point.
calc_financeira.impact: The evolution is demonstrable in both states, which is more useful than the end result alone.

aquila_e_evelyn.proves: No framework when the problem does not ask for one. And a clear split between private memory and public case: the original stayed preserved on a branch, the published version lost every event detail.
aquila_e_evelyn.context: A digital wedding invitation published as a showcase, with the private version preserved on an archive branch.
aquila_e_evelyn.constraint: The original carries guest and event data, which cannot go into a public repository.
aquila_e_evelyn.decision: Publish a sanitised edition and keep the original on a separate branch, instead of choosing between losing the evidence and exposing the data.
aquila_e_evelyn.impact: The visual work stays demonstrable without any event data becoming public.

presente_para_daniela.proves: Accessibility handled where almost nobody handles it: an animation-heavy site that honours prefers-reduced-motion shows the care is a habit, not a work checklist.
presente_para_daniela.context: A narrative experience with heavy animation, published as a sanitised edition with the original preserved on a historical branch.
presente_para_daniela.constraint: Strong animation causes real discomfort for people who asked the system for less motion.
presente_para_daniela.decision: Respect prefers-reduced-motion even in a project whose value lives in the animation, and sanitise the intimate content before publishing.
presente_para_daniela.impact: It is the only project here with art direction and narrative as a requirement, and it is still accessible.

dnd_augury_guide.proves: A deliberate choice not to use a framework where the content is static — no build step, no dependency tree to maintain. A maintenance-cost decision, not a taste one.
dnd_augury_guide.context: An interactive D&D guide as a static site, with races, classes, a character sheet and a gallery.
dnd_augury_guide.constraint: Static content justifies neither a build step nor a dependency tree to maintain afterwards.
dnd_augury_guide.decision: Ship with no framework and no build, using Bootstrap, in the same line as the client landings from the same period.
dnd_augury_guide.impact: The site is still serveable years later without reinstalling anything.
